assumptions.relaxation_effect: Exposure and diversion remain mechanisms of the policy's total casualty effect but prevent interpreting the total-count contrast as a per-trip or per-kilometre safety effect.

novelty_assessment.scope: This assessment concerns the Observatory's analysis of the challenged attribution claim, not the positive 28 percent claim as an endorsed result. It separates five contribution units: prior Wales causal evaluations and difference-in-differences designs; the general 20/30 mph reclassification issue; exact first-year graphic and source-vintage reconciliation; affected-road estimand separation; and the case-specific constructive point-and-sign non-identification witness. Correctness, publication readiness and historical priority are outside this novelty decision.

claim.natural_language: The Welsh default 20 mph limit caused the reported 28% fall in casualties on 20 and 30 mph roads in its first year.

identification.proof_summary: Exact arithmetic reproduces the provisional aggregate before-after change but does not reveal affected-road membership or the no-policy post outcome. The verified artifact gives all three worlds the same hypothetical observed decomposition: baseline 2,000 affected plus 402 other equals 2,402, and policy-post 1,000 affected plus 725 other equals 1,725. In World A the affected-road no-policy post count is 1,000, so the effect is 0%. In World B it is 2,000, so the effect is -50%. In World C it is 500, so the effect is +100%. Since identical observables are compatible with negative, zero and positive values of the exact registered estimand, neither the point nor its sign is identified. These illustrative values are not bounds, estimates or factual claims.
identification.scope: Producer-side determination for the preregistered first-year percent effect on affected Welsh road segments, using the frozen aggregate official corpus and admitted model class. It is not an independently reviewed determination and does not assess a future design with a historical treatment map or newly justified restrictions.

witness.statement: The exact witness constructs three hypothetical affected-road structural worlds with the same aggregate baseline count 2,402 and policy-post count 1,725. All share the same hypothetical observed decomposition, but the unobserved affected-road no-policy post count yields causal effects of 0%, -50% and +100%. Negative, zero and positive effects are therefore observationally equivalent in this design, proving that neither the point nor its sign is identified. None of the worlds is asserted to be true.

inferences.claim_ceiling: No sign, magnitude or zero/nonzero causal conclusion follows. The finding is nonidentification of this design, not evidence that the true effect is 0%, -50% or +100%.
inferences.derivation: The deterministic witness fixes a shared hypothetical observed decomposition: baseline 2,000 affected plus 402 other equals 2,402; policy-post 1,000 affected plus 725 other equals 1,725. World A sets the affected-road no-policy post count to 1,000, giving a 0% effect. World B sets it to 2,000, giving a -50% effect. World C sets it to 500, giving a +100% effect. All three map to the same available aggregate observations. The observation map is therefore non-injective with respect to the registered estimand, and the witnessed negative, zero and positive effects show that its sign is also not identified. The worlds are counterexamples, not claims about reality.
inferences.scope: Point identification of the preregistered first-year percent effect on affected road segments from the frozen aggregate before-after corpus and admitted unrestricted counterfactual class.
inferences.statement: The registered causal effect and its sign are non-identified from the available aggregate evidence: three exact hypothetical structural worlds reproduce the same observed aggregate baseline of 2,402 and post count of 1,725 but imply affected-road causal effects of 0%, -50% and +100%.

inferences.claim_ceiling: Do not report a causal confidence interval, identified interval, sign, minimum effect or maximum effect from this audit.

inferences.scope: The declared source-bounded model class only; additional externally justified restrictions could define a different identified set in a future version.
inferences.statement: The frozen design supplies no finite partial-identification interval and no sign restriction for the registered causal effect because no empirical bounds on the affected-road decomposition, no-policy trend, classification, ascertainment or exposure are registered.

novelty.assessment_scope: This assessment concerns the Observatory's analysis of the challenged attribution claim, not the positive 28 percent claim as an endorsed result. It separates five contribution units: prior Wales causal evaluations and difference-in-differences designs; the general 20/30 mph reclassification issue; exact first-year graphic and source-vintage reconciliation; affected-road estimand separation; and the case-specific constructive point-and-sign non-identification witness. Correctness, publication readiness and historical priority are outside this novelty decision.
novelty.residual_contribution: The broad Wales causal-evaluation and difference-in-differences claims collide, and posted-speed reclassification was already recognised. The residual is only a case- and corpus-specific BRIDGE: an exact frozen-vintage reconstruction of the reported first-year graphic, separation of the combined posted-speed proxy from the affected-road estimand, and an application of established identification theory that constructs observationally equivalent worlds with different causal signs. No exact Wales application of that registered witness was found in the bounded search completed on 11 August 2026; this is not a new theorem or an absolute priority claim.

mechanisms.causal_pathway: Background safety trends or transitory baseline variation change the post-period casualty count without a policy effect.
mechanisms.description: Casualties could change over time independently of the default speed-limit policy or after an unusually high comparison period.
distinguishing_measurements: Quarterly casualty series for affected segments and credible untreated units over a longer pre-policy period
Preregistered event-study pre-trends, alternative trend models and placebo intervention dates
A baseline-selection audit that does not condition on the observed post-policy result
mechanisms.exclusion_basis: Not excluded. The official long-run decline and divergent pre-policy donor placebo make a no-trend interpretation untenable without additional restrictions.
mechanisms.name: Secular casualty trend and regression to the mean

mechanisms.causal_pathway: A lower or differently composed exposure produces fewer recorded casualties even if conditional road-user risk is unchanged; policy-induced displacement can also move casualties between measured road groups.
mechanisms.description: Changes in vehicle kilometres, route choice, modal composition or trip timing could change casualty counts independently of a change in risk per unit of exposure.
distinguishing_measurements: Vehicle-kilometre and traffic-count series on affected, exception, comparison and spillover road segments
Road-user and vehicle composition by segment and period
A separately registered total-count, risk-rate and displacement decomposition
mechanisms.exclusion_basis: Not excluded. The available 1.3% traffic increase is an all-Wales calendar-year aggregate and cannot measure affected-segment exposure or diversion.
mechanisms.name: Traffic volume and composition change

mechanisms.causal_pathway: Measurement-system or category-membership change creates an apparent casualty change without an equivalent change in underlying harm on the registered affected segments.
mechanisms.description: Changes in police reporting, validation, severity coding, road speed-limit coding or inclusion rules could alter the measured series.
distinguishing_measurements: Frozen reporting definitions, revision histories and validation logs across periods
Stable-segment reanalysis with road-speed coding reconstructed from versioned local-authority records
Triangulation of police-recorded totals against independent ascertainment sources
mechanisms.exclusion_basis: Not excluded. Manual speed-limit corrections, unamended historical inconsistencies, general under-coverage and cross-vintage discrepancies remain material. The CRaSH change is not asserted to alter all-severity totals.
mechanisms.name: Reporting, coding or road-classification change

mechanisms.causal_pathway: Different weather or seasonal intensity changes casualties during the comparison windows independently of the policy, even though the four-quarter windows contain the same named quarters.
mechanisms.description: Weather and seasonal conditions can affect travel exposure, road conditions and collision risk.
distinguishing_measurements: Weather-adjusted segment-period models with frozen meteorological inputs
Same-quarter comparisons across several years and weather placebo checks
mechanisms.exclusion_basis: Not excluded. Matching quarter labels removes simple seasonal composition but not year-specific weather or exposure differences.
mechanisms.name: Weather and seasonality

mechanisms.causal_pathway: Concurrent interventions affect speed, collision probability, injury severity or recording and are attributed to the legal default if omitted.
mechanisms.description: Enforcement intensity, road engineering, public campaigns, vehicle safety or emergency-service changes could coincide with implementation.
distinguishing_measurements: Dated segment-period enforcement, engineering and campaign records
Designs that separate the legal default, its implementation package and unrelated interventions
mechanisms.exclusion_basis: Not excluded. The frozen corpus does not contain a complete segment-period intervention history.
mechanisms.name: Enforcement and concurrent road-safety interventions

mechanisms.causal_pathway: A nominally pre-policy reporting bin mixes untreated and treated days, while anticipation moves part of any response into earlier dates. This changes both the before/after contrast and its interpretation without identifying the registered affected-road counterfactual.
mechanisms.description: The whole-quarter comparison baseline ends in 2023 Q3 even though legal commencement was 17 September 2023, so it contains 14 post-implementation calendar days; announcement, preparation, enforcement messaging or early behaviour could also change outcomes before the legal date.
distinguishing_measurements: Daily or weekly affected-segment collision and casualty data spanning announcement, preparation and commencement
A registered event study separating anticipation, 17-30 September 2023 implementation days and the first four complete post-policy quarters
Correction logs split between 17-30 September 2023 and 2023 Q4, with stable road identifiers and original-versus-corrected speed codes
mechanisms.exclusion_basis: Not excluded. The frozen whole-quarter data cannot separate the 14 implementation days from the rest of 2023 Q3, the approximately 120 manual corrections cover 17 September through 31 December rather than the two bins separately, and the corpus contains no complete anticipation-period behaviour series.
mechanisms.name: Implementation-quarter contamination and behavioural anticipation

mechanisms.causal_pathway: Changing segment membership or spillover changes casualties in the reported aggregate without identifying the treated-road no-policy counterfactual.
mechanisms.description: The combined 20 mph and 30 mph series mixes changed and unchanged segments, while local exceptions, later changes and traffic diversion can alter membership or outcomes across boundaries.
distinguishing_measurements: Versioned treated, exempt and changed-back road-segment map linked to stable identifiers
Stable-boundary, exception-road and spillover-ring analyses with segment-level outcomes and exposure
mechanisms.exclusion_basis: Not excluded. The all-20-mph-plus-30-mph reporting scope is not the registered affected-segment population, and no frozen historical membership panel is available.
mechanisms.name: Road reclassification, local exceptions and spillover

limitations: The frozen corpus is predominantly official producer material and is not a systematic academic-literature review.
No versioned historical affected-segment map, segment-level traffic exposure, weather series or complete enforcement and engineering intervention history was available.
The England donor was not validated for parallel trends, stable composition, no interference or policy non-contamination.
The admitted rival set is deliberately preserved as non-exhaustive; absence of another documented rival is not evidence that none exists.
search_statement.method: Searched the frozen official Welsh Government, StatsWales, DfT and legislation corpus for claim wording, policy scope, measurement changes, revisions, long-run trends, traffic exposure, implementation timing, anticipation and alternative outcome patterns. Replayed the current quarterly Welsh series, DfT collision rows, an England donor diagnostic, a one-window-earlier pre-period diagnostic and outcome-category diagnostics. The search was adversarial and source-bounded; none of the diagnostics was treated as a causal estimate.

sensitivity_results.robustness_summary: The descriptive fall is sensitive to source vintage, and the donor differential is sensitive to outcome scope and unsupported comparison assumptions. Across the tested vintages and diagnostics, the producer-side NON_IDENTIFIED classification is unchanged because affected-road membership and the no-policy outcome remain latent. This is robustness only within the declared frozen checks, not proof against all future designs or evidence.
